outcome: Help media owners plan and deliver eligible advertising inventory that balances revenue, audience experience, brand safety and contractual obligations.
overview: Advertising inventory is fragmented across broadcast, streaming, audio and digital, and pacing is still managed by hand, so campaigns underdeliver, remnant stock is discounted late, frequency is uncontrolled and unsafe adjacencies slip through. This solution forecasts available inventory, allocates campaigns against contractual and consent rules, applies brand-safety and editorial gates before delivery, and rebalances pacing as actual delivery arrives. Reconciliation ties delivery to billing so disputes are evidenced rather than argued. A 6–10 week pilot on one inventory pool targets better fill and yield with fewer underdelivery penalties, measured through controlled experiments rather than assumed attribution.

benefits.text: Improve fill and yield on the pilot inventory pool, or reduce underdelivery against contracted volumes
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Validated only through controlled experiments on the customer’s own inventory; demand conditions and sales performance dominate outcomes — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Honour contractual, consent, frequency and brand-safety rules as hard constraints ahead of allocation
benefits.source: Architecture design — eligibility, consent and brand gates run before the yield and pacing layer
benefits.limits: Gate quality depends on the accuracy of contract terms, consent state and content classification

benefits.text: Cut campaign reporting and reconciliation effort by tying delivery records to billing automatically
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on ad-server and billing-system data quality and on agreed reconciliation rules

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); inventory, campaign, consent and delivery records remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs, with audience data handled in aggregate wherever the use case allows

notFor.situation: Inventory and delivery data cannot be obtained from the ad server at campaign granularity
notFor.why: Forecasting, pacing and reconciliation all depend on actual delivery records; without them the platform can only restate the plan

notFor.situation: There is no consent framework or lawful basis for audience-based targeting
notFor.why: Audience eligibility is enforced from consent state; without it the platform can optimise only contextual and contracted inventory

notFor.situation: Causal revenue claims are expected without experiments
notFor.why: Attribution without a holdout cannot separate the platform’s effect from demand and sales activity, and this record will not claim what it cannot measure

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns commercial policy, consent and brand-safety standards and every pricing decision · Duration: 6–10 week pilot; further 14–26 weeks to enterprise rollout
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, data engineer, optimisation engineer; customer yield owner, ad-operations lead, privacy reviewer, commercial finance lead · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery and baseline agreement
2) Inventory, contract and consent data preparation
3) Forecasting, gate and pacing build
4) Holdout experiment setup and reconciliation testing
5) Controlled launch on the pilot inventory pool
6) Stabilisation and handover
deliverables: Inventory, delivery and billing reconcile within the agreed tolerance
Consent, brand-safety and frequency rules pass the agreed test packs
Decision latency and throughput hold at peak load
Security and privacy review passed and commercial UAT complete

languages: Arabic and English campaign metadata, brand rules and reporting supported; delivery in English
